name: OZYMANDIA'S TENT

subjects.name: MADAME OZYMANDIA'S TABLE
LOOK_AT: A round table under a fringed cloth. Round, I am told, so that no one sits at the head. She sits at the head anyway.
The fringe is long enough to hide a foot. I'm choosing not to wonder whose.
A ring of wear on the cloth where a hundred clients have rested their hands, palms up, and paid.
LISTEN_TO: The cloth's tassels, moving without wind. There is a wind. It is just not one you can feel.
The tassels again, swaying. I checked for a draft. There is a draft.
Nothing, for once. The table is between appointments.

overrides.PULL: One came off in my hand. It was back on the cloth when I looked again. I've elected not to think about this.

subjects.name: THE CRYSTAL BALL
LOOK_AT: A glass ball on a brass stand. In it: the tent, upside down, and me, small. It is right about both.
Glass. Good glass, though. She hasn't economized on the glass.
A small chip on the underside, turned to the wall. Even the future has a bad side.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. Glass keeps what it sees.
Nothing. It is reflecting, which is quiet work.
A faint ring when the table is bumped. The future, briefly, in a key.

LOOK_AT: A glass ball. In it: the tent, upside down, and me, small, and apparently deceased. I look well, considering.

overrides.USE: I looked. Upside-down tent, small Thad. Two dollars. On reflection — which is all the ball does — fair.

subjects.name: THE BRASS ROD
LOOK_AT: A dowsing rod of solid brass, polished at the grip. It finds water, gold, and — per the sign — 'that which the seeker conceals from himself.' Priced accordingly.
A brass rod. Gold is not magnetic and neither is brass, and I have decided that raising this would be unkind and also expensive.
The grip is wrapped in red thread, worn through to the brass where her thumb goes. Eleven years of the same thumb.
LISTEN_TO: A hum, if I hold my breath. Possibly my own blood. Possibly not.
It rings when she sets it down. She sets it down a great deal, always in the same place, and it always rings the same.
Nothing, when I breathe normally. So I'm breathing normally.

overrides.USE: It swung toward the money box. 'It seeks the hidden metal,' she said, without a trace of embarrassment. Professional courtesy forbade comment.

subjects.name: THE PRICE LIST
LOOK_AT: Divination, two dollars. Boundary divination, two dollars. Consultation regarding prices, one dollar.
Below the prices, smaller: SATISFACTION AS THE SPIRITS ALLOW.
Boundary divination costs the same as the ordinary kind. The earth does not charge extra for lines, apparently.
LISTEN_TO: Paper. The prices hold steady, which is more than the bank manages.
Nothing.
The card tapping against the tent pole in the draft. Two dollars, two dollars.

subjects.name: THE CARDS
LOOK_AT: A deck worn soft, wrapped in silk. The top card, when she is elsewhere, is always the same one. I've stopped checking which.
The silk has a monogram, faded past reading. They were somebody else's before they were hers.
The deck is thinner than a full deck. Some futures, she says, are not for sale.
LISTEN_TO: Card against card, in the wrap. They shuffle themselves slightly. I have decided this is settling.
A whisper of silk when the tent breathes.
Nothing. They are waiting to be told what they mean.

overrides.PICK_UP: The silk wrap tightened. I didn't see her move. The deck stayed where destiny — her word — had left it.

subjects.name: THE TEA SERVICE
LOOK_AT: The leaves are read in a cup with no handle, from a pot that is never empty. The tea itself is genuinely good, which she considers beside the point.
The cups are four different patterns, each from a different town she has left.
The leaves at the bottom of my cup made a shape. I asked what it was. She said it was a fee.
LISTEN_TO: The pot, at a murmur. It is always just off the boil.
A soft rattle of china when the table moves.
The pot, still murmuring. It is the only thing in the tent that never pretends.

subjects.name: THE INCENSE BURNER
LOOK_AT: Smoke rises from it in a line and then decides things. The smell is cedar, church, and somewhere behind both, supper.
It is shaped like a small brass temple from a country she has certainly never seen.
The ash beneath it is a week deep. The smell of the tent is mostly the tent's own history.
LISTEN_TO: The faintest crackle. A very small fire with a very large job.
A thread of smoke whispering as it breaks against the canvas.
Nothing between draws, then the faint crackle again, working.

subjects.name: THE TENT WALLS
LOOK_AT: Canvas, painted with stars on the inside, patched with flour sacks on the out. From in here, the sky is always clear.
Some of the painted stars are in constellations. Some are wherever she wanted a star.
From outside: FLOUR, FLOUR, FLOUR, in faded stencil. From inside: the heavens.
LISTEN_TO: Canvas breathing. The whole room inhales.
A gust leaning on the canvas, and the stars bellying in.
The street through canvas, soft and far, like a rumor about a street.

subjects.name: THE TESTIMONIAL BOARD
LOOK_AT: Letters pinned up: SHE FOUND MY RING. SHE KNEW ABOUT WILLIAM. One reads only I WAS WRONG TO DOUBT, unsigned, in a fine hand.
Letters of thanks. They are in four different hands and one of them is hers.
I WAS WRONG TO DOUBT is pinned higher than the others, at eye level. She knows which letter does the work.
LISTEN_TO: Paper, pinned and fluttering. A choir of the convinced.
Nothing.
A pin working loose, and a letter sliding an inch before it holds. Even the convinced waver.

subjects.name: THE LANTERN, RED
LOOK_AT: A lantern with red glass, hung center. It makes everyone's face look like a secret being kept.
The red glass is cracked and mended with a strip of red ribbon. Nothing in here is allowed to be ordinary, not even a repair.
Under it my hands look like a stranger's, and a lucky one.
LISTEN_TO: The flame, steady. Red does not flicker, apparently. Ask her why.
A faint hiss from the wick. Steady, as advertised.
Nothing. The red keeps the flame quiet, or she does.

subjects.name: THE MONEY BOX
LOOK_AT: A cash box with a painted eye on the lid. Nobody steals from it. The eye may be why. The eye may not be why.
The eye on the lid has been repainted. It used to look left. It now looks at you.
A slot in the top and no lock. It does not need one.
LISTEN_TO: Coins, when the table moves. She is doing better than the Mercantile.
Nothing. It's listening to me, possibly.
A single coin shifting as she passes the table. It knows its owner.

overrides.OPEN: The painted eye and I held a discussion. The eye won on experience.

subjects.name: THE FLAP TO OUTSIDE
LOOK_AT: The tent flap, weighted so it closes itself with a certain finality. Entrances here are hers; exits are yours.
Small bells are sewn along the hem. They ring when you leave, never when you come in.
The weights in the hem are horseshoes, four of them. Luck, put to practical use.
LISTEN_TO: The street, arriving in pieces. She hears all of this, all day. Perhaps that is the whole trick.
The bells on the hem, faintly, in the wind.
The street, and then the flap closing it off with a soft and final thump.

subjects.name: THE CHART
LOOK_AT: A chart of the humors of the earth, hand-painted, extremely detailed, and entirely invented. It took somebody weeks.
The earth's humors are color-coded. Gold is a warm humor. Debt, I notice, is not on it.
In one corner, very small, the painter's name. It is hers, in a different style.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing.
Nothing. Invented things make no noise.
The paper lifting at one corner in the draft from the flap.

LOOK_AT: A chart of the humors of the earth, entirely invented, and it took somebody weeks. In this town that's practically a founding document.

subjects.name: THE SECOND ROD
LOOK_AT: An identical rod, in a box, under the table. She has a spare. I find this oddly reassuring about her sincerity.
The box is lined in velvet and the spare is polished. It has never been used, and it is better looked after than the first.
Two rods. If one finds nothing, there is always the other, to find nothing in agreement.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing, boxed.
Nothing, under the table, in the dark.
A faint ring when the table is bumped. It would like to work.

subjects.name: THE GROUND
LOOK_AT: Bare earth, under a tent, in the middle of town. She could have had a floor. She has chosen not to have a floor.
Swept bare and level, with the marks of a broom going round in circles, like the rest of the business.
Her chair legs have sunk an inch into it. She has sat in exactly the same place for a very long time.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing unusual.
Nothing unusual. Earth, under a tent.
Nothing. Packed dirt, minding its own business.

subjects.name: THE CUSHIONS
LOOK_AT: Cushions on the client's side, faded velvet, each softer than the last. You sink into a consultation.
There's a coin down between two of them. I've left it. It's probably part of the act.
Her side has no cushion, only a hard stool. She does not need to be comfortable to be certain.
LISTEN_TO: A soft sigh of velvet as I lean on one.
Nothing. They absorb everything, including doubt.
A faint crunch of something sewn inside. Lavender, or nerves.

subjects.name: THE STOVE
LOOK_AT: A small iron stove, very hot, in a tent whose door is a sheet of canvas.
It is fed with pages from an almanac. The future, she tells me, is excellent fuel.
The heat makes the painted stars shimmer. I'm almost certain that's deliberate.
LISTEN_TO: A low roar, small and steady, like an audience waiting.
A page curling as it catches.
Iron ticking. It keeps better time than her predictions.

subjects.name: THE CURTAIN
LOOK_AT: A curtain at the back, dark velvet with a fringe of gold thread, most of it still gold.
Behind it, she says, the spirits wait. Behind it, I am fairly sure, is her bed.
It is drawn exactly as far as she wants it drawn. I have never seen it move, and I have never seen it in the same place twice.
LISTEN_TO: Breathing behind it, or the tent breathing. I prefer the tent.
Nothing behind the curtain. The spirits are between appointments.
The rings on the rail, faintly, when the wind leans on the tent.

subjects.name: THE SÉANCE TABLE
LOOK_AT: A round table under a cloth that reaches the floor on every side. Whatever goes on under there is between it and the spirits.
Five chairs, five townspeople, five two-dollar faces. There is no sixth chair, and plenty of room underneath.
In the middle, one candle and a little bell, for spirits who would rather ring.
LISTEN_TO: Ten feet shifting under the cloth. There would be room for two more.
Somebody's knee has found the table leg, and apologizes to it.
Nothing, which at a séance is the main attraction.

overrides.PULL: If I pull the cloth, the spirits get a candle in their lap, and so does Mr. Frame.
overrides.PICK_UP: It has five people holding on to it. Six, if you count the dead.

subjects.name: THE LAMP
LOOK_AT: A hanging lamp, turned up. Madame Ozymandia keeps the dead in good light until the money is in.
It throws the whole table's shadow on the canvas. Mine would be the shadow of a man who has not paid.
The wick is trimmed for a long evening. The spirits, I expect, are billed by the hour.
LISTEN_TO: A soft hiss, like somebody keeping a secret badly.
Moths at the glass, wanting in, in the way of moths.
The flame steadies. Nobody has breathed for a while.

overrides.USE: It is hers. She would charge me for the dark.
overrides.PULL: Pulling it down would end the séance, and then I would have to explain the séance.

subjects.name: THE SITTERS
LOOK_AT: Four of the town in their good coats, holding hands. They have paid two dollars each to meet a man they have only read about.
One of them has brought her question on a slip of paper, in case the dead are hard of hearing.
They are watching the candle. I could be anybody, and tonight I would rather be.
LISTEN_TO: Somebody whispers that Mott will know where the gold is. Somebody else whispers that he never did.
A stomach, and then an apology to the spirits for it.
Four people trying to breathe quietly, which is louder than breathing.

overrides.TALK_TO: One of them puts a finger to her lips. The spirits are shy, she implies, and so should I be.
overrides.USE: There is no sixth chair. I could stand at the back, and be charged for standing.
overrides.PICK_UP: They are holding hands. They would come as a set.

subjects.name: MR. FRAME, AT THE TABLE
LOOK_AT: Mr. Frame, front row, pencil ready. He has written the headline already and left a space for whatever the dead say.
His notebook is open at a fresh page headed MOTT SPEAKS. It is a very confident page.
He is the only one at the table not holding hands. He needs both of them to write.
LISTEN_TO: His pencil, tapping the page, impatient for the hereafter.
He whispers a headline to himself, tries a second, and prefers the first.
Nothing. Mr. Frame, silent, is the strangest thing in the tent.

subjects.name: MADAME OZYMANDIA, PRESIDING
LOOK_AT: Madame Ozymandia at the head of the table, in more scarves than usual, the brass rod across her palms.
Her eyes are closed. One of them is not entirely closed, and it is on the money box.
She has the air of a woman to whom the dead owe money.
LISTEN_TO: She hums, low, a note that is neither music nor not.
Coins settling in the box at her feet, a sound she seems to find restful.
Nothing. She is listening, which she tells me is new.

overrides.PULL: If I take the rod, she will have to listen with her hands, and she charges extra for that.
overrides.PICK_UP: She would charge me for the lift.

subjects.name: THE STAKE
LOOK_AT: A post with a dot on it, at the corner of my claim. On paper it is the most definite thing I own.
Somebody drew it with one stroke and did not go back. I know the feeling.
The stake. Everything I have starts there, thereabouts.
LISTEN_TO: Paper, under the tip of the rod. A dry little scratch.
Madame Ozymandia, humming on one note. It is nearly an A, and nearly is the trouble.
Nothing from the stake. It has made its point.

subjects.name: THE SLOPE
LOOK_AT: Hatching, to show the ground going up. The draughtsman tired about halfway, and so, I expect, does the hill.
Uphill of my claim, in pencil. It looks steeper drawn than I hope it is walked.
A good deal of slope with nothing on it. That is what the Company calls prospect.
LISTEN_TO: The rod's tip, crossing the hatching. It ticks on every stroke, like a stick along a fence.
Her bracelets, when she leans in. The earth's voice has a quantity of brass in it.
Nothing. Drawn hills are quiet. I have no evidence about the real one.

subjects.name: THE LARGER ROCK
LOOK_AT: The larger of two rocks. It has been drawn with shading, which the other has not. Rank tells, even in geology.
A rock, on a map, where a careful man would put a monument. This district puts rocks.
It is the only thing above my claim with a shadow. I take it for a landmark, having no choice.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. It is a drawing of a rock, and has the reticence of both.
The lamp, ticking overhead. The rock makes no comment.
Her humming goes up a little when the rod comes near it. I think she likes this one.

subjects.name: THE SMALLER ROCK
LOOK_AT: The smaller rock. It sits a little apart, like a man who was not asked.
No shading. Whoever drew this map had a favorite, and this was not it.
It is hardly a rock. In fairness, I am hardly a prospector.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing, and from the smaller rock I had expected less.
The humming drops when the rod passes over it. Even the earth cannot spare it the time.
Nothing. It is being brave about it.

subjects.name: CLAIM ONE
LOOK_AT: Claim One. Beside mine, and the same size, and nobody has circled it.
A square with a 1 in it. It got here first, which in this territory is most of the law.
It shares a line with mine. I have looked for a difference between the two, and the map does not record one.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. A numeral in a box.
The rod goes quiet over it, or she does. With her I cannot always tell which.
Nothing. Whatever is said about Claim One is not said on this map.

subjects.name: CLAIM TWO
LOOK_AT: Claim Two, in a red circle. Somebody marked it before I ever came, and I should like to know whether that is a welcome or a target.
A square with a 2 in it. I paid four dollars and a watch for that numeral.
Prosperity, from above. It looks drier.
LISTEN_TO: The red ink has a ridge to it. The rod catches on my own claim.
Her humming, steady, directly over my property. I am being billed for that.
Nothing. At this scale my mud is silent, which is an improvement.

subjects.name: THE CREEK
LOOK_AT: The creek, in three wavering lines. It is the best-drawn thing on the sheet, and it is leaving.
It runs past the foot of both claims and stops for neither.
A creek and, beyond it, a road. Two ways out of the district, drawn with great care.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. She does not hum over water. I gather it interferes.
The rod, crossing the lines. Three ticks, like a man counting his change.
Nothing. It is a drawing of a noise.

MADAME OZYMANDIA.PICK_UP: There would be a fee, and then a curse, and the fee would be larger.
MADAME OZYMANDIA.PUSH: She would sway, theatrically, and describe it afterward as a vision.
MADAME OZYMANDIA.GIVE: Anything I give her, she prices.
